parts: Hi Karl. Thank you for great lectures at the Course on Systems Genetics! I am trying to convert raw megaMUGA data (that come as two files - one is with genotypes and the second one with marker annotations) to an input file for rqtl. Is there a software that can covert these data in one of the input file formats?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] megaMUGA raw data conversion into a format accaptable for rqtl

I don't think there is software available to do the data transformation.
I think you'd need to write a special script, in a language like Python, Perl, or Ruby.

karl

parts:
Andrei

I can confirm this and recommend you also take into consideration
that, depending on your project, many of the SNPs returned from
geneseek are uninformative if you are doing a diallele cross while
others do poorly as indicated by the confidence calls on the data
output. As long as you are formating for Rqtl, you may as well deal
with these issues at the same time (provided you can find the
appropriate person to filter/transform the dataset). This is quite
simple for most bioinformatics groups.

Related to this, after having a such a transformation done by a local
collaborator followed by converting the position from Base pair to cM
at http://cgd.jax.org/mousemapconverter/, we found that while these
markers were still in the correct order the estimated positions in cM
were further off as we went down the Chromosomes... Is there a better
tool for making these conversions?

Bruce

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: megaMUGA raw data conversion into a format accaptable for rqtl
parts:
The cM positions from the MouseMapConverter are a good starting point, but if you have a reasonably large cross, you'd probably want to use the genetic map estimated from your own data.

Genetic maps vary by sex and strain, but I think the Cox et al. map is currently the best reference for the mouse.

karl
